source.title: Triple Phase Transitions: Understanding the Learning Dynamics of Large Language Models from a Neuroscience Perspective
source.authors: Yuko Nakagi; Keigo Tada; S. Yoshino; Shinji Nishimoto; Yu Takagi

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream benchmark performance across training checkpoints and training-token counts, bearing on V6, but does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream task accuracy over training checkpoints and tokens, which bears on V6. Its brain-encoding and probing measures do not measure the claim versions. References to scaling-law papers are background citations, not results from this study. It does not test power-law loss scaling, small-run extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture sensitivity of loss, other modalities or regimes, or fitting dependence.
record.test_reason: The study tracks 5-shot benchmark accuracy (MMLU, CSQA, ARC, HellaSwag) across 18–28 pretraining checkpoints of four ~7B models. That gives downstream performance as a function of training tokens, which bears on V6. It is a new setting (checkpoint trajectories) aimed at phase transitions, not at testing scaling laws. It fits no loss curves and does not vary model size. Brain-encoding and probing measures do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that encoding, probing and benchmark accuracy change together through three phases common across models: alignment with instruction following, detachment with stagnation, and realignment with consolidation. These phases appear only for languages well represented in training. They frame this as emergent or phase-transition dynamics, not as a scaling law. They do not discuss predictability of downstream performance.
record.recipe_differences: Tracks benchmark accuracy, probing, and brain encoding across pretrained-model checkpoints; does not fit held-out loss scaling laws or conduct compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported phase pattern depends on whether the input language is one the model learned; it is not observed for the tested untrained Chinese condition. Amber's downstream performance reaches only instruction-following.

fits_no_version.finding: Brain-encoding accuracy (fMRI alignment) rises, falls, then rises again over training tokens. It tracks the intrinsic dimension of activations rather than growing monotonically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Brain alignment of LM representations changes non-monotonically with pretraining tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probing accuracy for task answer labels rises sharply in later layers after about 3e11 tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-relevant internal representations emerge abruptly late in pretraining.

record.code_released: The authors say source code and training data will be made public on acceptance; no released URL is stated.
record.problems: Benchmark values are presented in figures without numerical scores or reported uncertainty. The study does not evaluate predictive fits, held-out pretraining loss, or compute-optimal scaling.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fits in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits and no extrapolation to larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep and no allocation of parameters versus tokens.
Architectures differ across the models, but their loss is not compared at fixed size.
No other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer regimes.
No relation of accuracy to pretraining loss. No variation in model size (all models are 6.7–7.3B). No forecasting or curve fitting; only token-count trajectories within single runs.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: MMLU benchmark accuracy for OLMo-2 and OLMo-0724 on Japanese, a language they did not learn sufficiently. The text says the three-phase dynamics appear only for learned languages.

Whether Figure 2's benchmark line is the model's final output or Logit Lens accuracy at the selected layer (25 or 30). Appendix A.6/B.5 compute layer-wise benchmark accuracy, and the caption says layers were selected.

record.verdict_notes: The benchmark values are figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty, so all V6 states rest on the authors' descriptions. Scale varies only by training tokens within single runs of about 7B models, and checkpoints before 1e9 tokens exist only for LLM-jp. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as background for gradual abilities. The checkpoint layer and the choice of benchmark-accuracy layer may shape the visible plateau, which is why the second missing entry should be resolved.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss and power-law relationships with parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
The models have architectural differences, but the study does not compare their loss at fixed parameter count to test architecture sensitivity.
No other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer evaluation.
No explicit forecasting procedure or relation to pretraining loss is evaluated; results concern benchmark accuracy across training checkpoints and tokens.
No comparison of scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or curve forms.

relationships.condition: OLMo-2, OLMo-0724 and LLM-jp on languages they were trained on (English; English and Japanese for LLM-jp), MMLU and alternate tasks
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises overall with training tokens but in stages. It surges at about 1e9–1e10 tokens, stagnates from about 1e10 to 3e11 tokens, then rises sharply. This is not a smooth predictable trend (r1–r4, r8–r16; figure-only).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy surged around 10^9–10^10 tokens, stagnated from roughly 10^10 to 3×10^11 tokens, and then rose sharply.

relationships.reason: Benchmark gains stop at the instruction-following stage, with no late consolidation rise up to 1.26T tokens (r5).
relationships.display_finding: Gains stopped at the instruction-following stage, with no later consolidation increase through 1.26T tokens.

relationships.condition: Input language the model was not trained on (OLMo-2 on Chinese MMLU)
relationships.reason: The phase pattern, including the benchmark gains, is reported as not observed. Gains with tokens depend on the training language (r7; figure-only).
relationships.display_finding: The phase pattern and associated benchmark gains did not appear when OLMo-2 was evaluated in Chinese.

reader_labels.reason: Accuracy follows a staged trajectory with an initial surge, a prolonged stagnation, and a later rise rather than a uniformly increasing curve; the text reports similar dynamics across the principal models and alternate tasks (r1–r6, r8–r16).
